title: Adobe Premiere Pro Advanced Core v1

domain.name: Adobe Premiere Pro Advanced
domain.description: Advanced editorial workflows, multicam, audio, graphics, color, relinking, performance, and delivery in Premiere Pro. Exact menu locations and version-specific UI details belong in Current Intelligence.

competencies.name: Project & Media Organization
competencies.description: Organize complex Premiere projects for speed, handoff, and recovery.
competencies.purpose: Keep large edits understandable and resilient.

units.title: Project organization workflow
units.content: Create a deliberate bin structure, naming convention, sequence hierarchy, scratch/cache plan, and handoff notes before complexity grows.

units.title: Organize around retrieval
units.content: A good project structure minimizes the time needed to answer where an asset came from, which sequence is current, and what is safe to delete or archive.

units.title: Project organization failures
units.content: Avoid ambiguous sequence names, mixed camera originals and exports, uncontrolled autosave locations, duplicate media with unknown provenance, and destructive cleanup before verification.

drills.title: Audit a messy Premiere project
drills.prompt: Given a project with duplicate sequences, mixed exports, missing media, and unlabeled versions, propose a cleanup and handoff plan.

competencies.name: Advanced Editing & Trim Control
competencies.description: Use trim, ripple/roll, replace, nesting, and sequence structure intentionally.
competencies.purpose: Edit quickly without losing sync or story continuity.

units.title: Trims change relationships
units.content: Ripple, roll, slip, and slide edits change different relationships between clip content, neighboring cuts, and timeline duration; choose the operation that matches the intended story change.

units.title: Precision trim workflow
units.content: Identify the exact storytelling problem, choose the least disruptive trim type, protect sync and linked audio, review around the edit, then confirm downstream timing and graphics.

units.title: Trim failures
units.content: Avoid solving timing problems with unnecessary cuts, breaking sync, stacking fixes across nested sequences without tracing dependencies, and trimming before identifying which side of the edit should move.

drills.title: Choose the correct trim operation
drills.prompt: For several timeline problems, choose ripple, roll, slip, slide, replace, or no trim and explain the effect.

competencies.name: Multicam & Multi-Source Editing
competencies.description: Build and manage synchronized multicamera edits with reliable source relationships.
competencies.purpose: Handle events, interviews, and performance coverage efficiently.

units.title: Multicam workflow
units.content: Verify camera/audio clocks and metadata where available; choose sync strategy; build or validate the multicam source; label angles; monitor audio source policy; cut for story first and polish angle timing second.

units.title: Audio can be the timeline spine
units.content: When picture sources drift or differ, a stable master audio recording can provide the most reliable editorial reference.

units.title: Multicam failures
units.content: Avoid committing to bad sync, switching audio unintentionally with picture, ignoring drift on long recordings, and flattening multicam before the edit is truly stable.

drills.title: Build an event multicam plan
drills.prompt: Design a multicam setup for three cameras plus external audio across a long event.

competencies.name: Premiere Audio Mixing & Repair
competencies.description: Edit dialogue, music, ambience, and effects into a controlled mix inside Premiere.
competencies.purpose: Produce clear, balanced edits before specialist audio handoff when needed.

units.title: Editorial mix workflow
units.content: Set clip gain before heavy processing; clean dialogue conservatively; balance dialogue, music, ambience, and effects; use buses/submix logic where appropriate; automate changes; check peaks and loudness targets for the delivery context.

units.title: Fix source level before processor level
units.content: Normalize the gain structure before stacking compressors and limiters; processors behave better when the signal entering them is sensible.

units.title: Audio mixing failures
units.content: Avoid solving every level problem with compression, over-noise-reducing speech, letting music mask dialogue, and judging the mix only on one playback system.

drills.title: Mix a 60-second commercial
drills.prompt: Plan dialogue, music, effects, gain staging, and loudness checks for a short ad.

competencies.name: Essential Graphics, MOGRT & Template Systems
competencies.description: Use reusable graphic systems without turning edits into brittle one-off timelines.
competencies.purpose: Scale titles, lower thirds, captions, and branded graphics consistently.

units.title: Templates separate design from instances
units.content: Reusable graphics should expose the few controls editors need while protecting core brand structure.

units.title: Graphic template workflow
units.content: Define typography, spacing, motion, color, and editable fields; create or use a reusable template; test long/short content; verify safe areas and accessibility; document variant rules.

units.title: Template failures
units.content: Avoid hard-coded text spacing, inaccessible contrast, animations tied to one exact duration, and dozens of manually copied title layers with inconsistent styling.

drills.title: Design a reusable lower-third system
drills.prompt: Specify a branded lower-third system with editable fields and edge cases.

competencies.name: Premiere Color Workflow
competencies.description: Perform editorial color correction and controlled looks while preserving a clean handoff path.
competencies.purpose: Keep color decisions consistent without confusing correction, creative look, and display transforms.

units.title: Correction, look, and transform are different jobs
units.content: Exposure and balance, creative styling, and technical display/color-space transforms should be treated separately so problems can be diagnosed and handed off cleanly.

units.title: Editorial color pass
units.content: Confirm source interpretation; normalize exposure and white balance; match shots; protect skin and key brand colors; apply creative look intentionally; review scopes; verify export color behavior.

units.title: Color workflow failures
units.content: Avoid grading monitor appearance alone, stacking LUTs without knowing their role, correcting after an unintended transform, and using one global adjustment to hide shot-to-shot mismatches.

drills.title: Match a mixed-camera sequence
drills.prompt: Plan an editorial color pass for mixed cameras under changing light.

competencies.name: Relinking, Proxies & Performance
competencies.description: Use proxies, cache, relinking, and media management without damaging source relationships.
competencies.purpose: Keep demanding projects responsive and recoverable.

units.title: Proxy and relink workflow
units.content: Preserve original media paths and metadata; create proxies with reliable attachment rules; validate representative clips; relink by stable identifiers; keep cache disposable and source media authoritative.

units.title: Cache is disposable, provenance is not
units.content: Render files and cache can usually be rebuilt; original media identity, timecode, filenames, and verified relink relationships must be protected.

units.title: Performance workflow failures
units.content: Avoid renaming originals mid-project without a plan, relinking by approximate filenames, treating cache as source, and transcoding away metadata required for conform.

drills.title: Recover an offline project
drills.prompt: Given moved media, stale proxies, and a new drive layout, build a safe relink sequence.

competencies.name: Mastering, Export & Delivery QC
competencies.description: Create reliable masters and derivatives with deliberate codec, resolution, audio, caption, and verification choices.
competencies.purpose: Deliver files that meet platform or client requirements and remain reusable.

units.title: Delivery workflow
units.content: Start from the approved sequence; identify master and derivative needs; set frame size/rate, codec, bitrate, color, audio, and caption requirements; export; inspect full metadata and spot-check picture/audio; archive the master and settings.

units.title: Make one trustworthy master before many derivatives
units.content: A verified high-quality master gives later platform encodes a stable source and simplifies troubleshooting.

units.title: Export failures
units.content: Avoid guessing platform specs from old presets, exporting from an unapproved sequence, mixing frame-rate conversions casually, clipping audio, and delivering without opening the actual exported file.

drills.title: Plan a master and social derivative set
drills.prompt: Define export and QC for a master plus vertical, square, and web derivatives.
